page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v7 is a general-purpose instance configuration running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance supplies 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector mathematics and integer cryptography operations. System memory totals 128.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional single-threaded performance, with single-core stress-ng execution and bzip3 decompression achieving top-tier ratings in the top 10% of tested systems. PassMark CPU and memory benchmarks also position the machine in the upper 25th percentile. In contrast, aggregate parallel scaling drops to average levels, as multi-core stress-ng tests, Redis SET transactions at 47.72 million operations per second, and static web serving stay within the middle 50% performance bracket. While execution of smaller language models yields rapid inference, throughput on large 70B parameter models degrades significantly without hardware acceleration.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage, which necessitates network-attached Premium Storage or Azure managed disks for persistence and paging. There are no included graphics processing units. In terms of cost efficiency, the instance provides high compute density and capable single-thread throughput for its core count, but operators must factor in external storage costs when architecting stateful systems.

Microsoft Azure D32as_v7 is best aligned with enterprise applications requiring robust per-core execution speed and a balanced compute-to-memory footprint. Representative deployments include web application servers, relational database management systems reliant on remote block storage, compilation and continuous integration pipelines, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32as_v7 is a general-purpose cloud instance offering 32 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory on dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 hardware running at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 16 physical cores utilizing multithreading and supports AVX-512 vector instructions alongside cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage configurations, and features zero onboard GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong memory bandwidth, though parallel scaling across Redis transactions, multi-threaded decompression, and web throughput settles within mid-tier bounds. This resource profile delivers efficient compute allocation for balanced enterprise workloads, such as enterprise web serving, backend application runtimes, CI/CD compilation, and distributed database nodes operating over managed remote storage.
